projects.name: InCloseMail
projects.description: Desktop email for personal inboxes and Microsoft 365 business accounts.
projects.tagline: An Outlook alternative built for the desktop.
projects.featureText: Use it with personal inboxes and Microsoft 365 business accounts. Free for personal email, with paid plans for business accounts.
projects.longDescription:
InCloseMail was checked against classic Outlook screen by screen: the ribbon, folder pane, reading pane and To-Do Bar, Outlook's keyboard shortcuts and right-click menus, .pst import and export, rules and Quick Steps, calendar, people and tasks, shared mailboxes and Microsoft 365 Groups.

It adds things Outlook doesn't have: AI agents such as Claude can read and draft mail in the mailboxes you choose, Clean Up My Inbox sorts thousands of messages into groups you can act on at once, you can change any keyboard shortcut, and it keeps working offline during a Microsoft 365 outage.

It is free forever for Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live and other personal Microsoft accounts. Microsoft 365 work accounts will cost $3 per user per month ($36 a year) after the beta, and are free during it. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) and Windows 11.

projects.name: DesktopWiki
projects.description: A wiki for internal docs and team knowledge, with a free single-user tier.
projects.tagline: A team wiki that runs on your own PC.
projects.featureText: Spaces, a page tree and a visual editor, plus a password manager, with no server or cloud account to set up. Free for one person, with paid plans for families and teams.
projects.longDescription:
DesktopWiki gives a family or small team spaces, a page tree and a visual editor, the way classic team wikis work, plus a password manager for everyone's logins. You install it on one Windows PC, and everyone else opens it in a browser on a phone or another computer.

There is no server, database or cloud account to set up: the whole wiki lives in one file you can back up by copying it. It can import from Confluence and can be opened up for use away from home.

It is free for one person. Family (up to 6 people) is $49 a year, Team (up to 18) $99 and Business (up to 60) $199, on sale after the beta, with every feature in every plan. The host PC needs 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) or Windows 11.

projects.name: macshot
projects.alternative: Alternative to the macOS screenshot tool
projects.description: Capture, annotate, and record your screen. Includes scrolling capture and text recognition.
projects.longDescription:
macshot lives in the Mac menu bar. One hotkey freezes the screen so you can select a region, mark it up with arrows, text, shapes, numbered markers or blur, and copy it straight to the clipboard.

It also records the screen as MP4 or GIF with system audio and microphone, stitches scrolling captures into one tall image, reads text with OCR, can auto-redact emails, phone numbers and card numbers, and uploads to Google Drive, imgbb or any S3-compatible storage. It is a native Swift and AppKit app, also installable with Homebrew (brew install --cask macshot).
projects.builtWithAI: The macshot repo includes CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md instruction files for AI coding agents, and its commit history shows AI help: 37 of its 1,052 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude and 5 by Cursor. Most of the code is credited to its developer, sw33tLie.

projects.name: Locode
projects.description: Build React web apps from prompts using local Ollama models on an Apple Silicon Mac.
projects.longDescription:
Describe an app in plain English and Locode generates a complete React, Tailwind and Vite project, tests it with Playwright, fixes errors and lets you keep refining it with follow-up prompts. Everything runs on your own machine through Ollama, so there are no API keys or subscriptions.

The ready-made download is a DMG for Apple Silicon Macs. It can also be run from source with Python and Node.

projects.name: Glance
projects.description: Host and share previews of pages built by coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
projects.longDescription:
Glance lets a coding agent publish a page, dashboard or app to a live URL with one command (glance deploy). You leave comments on the page in the browser, much like in a Google Doc, and the agent reads them and fixes the page.

You host it yourself on Cloudflare's free tier. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cline, Aider or any agent that can run a shell command, every link needs a login, and optional Slack notifications tell you about new comments.

projects.name: FreeFlow
projects.description: Free voice dictation for your computer. Speak and it types for you, with no monthly subscription.
projects.builtWithAI: Zach Latta's original README (February 2026) said he "vibe-coded" FreeFlow over a weekend. The project keeps an AGENTS.md file for AI coding agents, and 97 of its 511 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude.
projects.longDescription:
Hold the Fn key, talk, and FreeFlow types what you said into whatever text field you are in. It cleans up filler words and spelling using nearby app context and your own vocabulary list, and Edit Mode can rewrite selected text from a spoken instruction such as "make this shorter".

It uses a free Groq API key by default, or any OpenAI-compatible provider including local models through Ollama or LM Studio. There is no FreeFlow server. It works on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

whatPeopleSay.summary: FreeFlow got a well-received Show HN launch, where people liked having a free alternative to paid dictation apps such as Wispr Flow and Superwhisper. Commenters pointed out that it only runs on macOS and that it sends audio to a cloud model rather than transcribing on the device, and many used the thread to compare it with local tools like Handy. Beyond that thread and a short positive write-up, coverage is thin.

projects.name: Open Source Barware
projects.alternative: Alternative to paid bar inventory software
projects.description: Local-first bar inventory software for counting stock and tracking usage, licensed GPLv3.
projects.longDescription:
Walk your shelves and say what you see ("Tito's, half. Jameson, full.") and Open Source Barware builds the count sheet, prices every bottle and tells you what's short and what to reorder. Import last week's sales from your POS and it flags bottles that came up short.

It runs on your own Mac or Windows laptop, works without internet or AI (AI is optional, for reading invoice photos), counts in English or Spanish and can run several locations. There is a sample bar to try in the browser. It is free with no paid tier, under GPLv3.
projects.builtWithAI: The maker says AI is what let people from the bar trade build the tool themselves. The GitHub repo keeps CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files for AI coding agents, and 56 of its 249 commits (checked 2026-11-22) are co-authored by Claude.

A Product Hunt launch drew only a handful of upvotes and one positive comment.

projects.longDescription:
Type a task the way you say it ("Call Sarah next Wed 3pm #work p1") and OpenTodo sets the date, project and priority. Today shows what is due, you can drag tasks onto a day or week calendar to block out time, and Focus runs a Pomodoro or countdown timer that logs time to the task. Lists can be shared with family or a team, and it works offline.

You run the server yourself (Docker, a single binary for Windows, Mac or Linux, Unraid, Home Assistant and more) or rent a hosted copy from PikaPods. There is an iPhone and iPad app in the App Store and an Android APK. Everything is free, with no paid tier.

projects.alternative: Alternative to ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow
projects.description: A local AI voice studio: clone a voice from a few seconds of audio, generate speech in 23 languages, and dictate into any app with a hotkey. Everything runs on your own computer.
projects.longDescription:
Voicebox covers both halves of voice: speech out, like ElevenLabs, and dictation in, like Wispr Flow. It has eight text-to-speech engines, zero-shot voice cloning and 50+ preset voices, effects such as pitch, reverb and compression, and no length limit. A global hotkey transcribes your speech with Whisper and pastes it into whatever you are typing in. Its MCP server lets AI agents such as Claude Code or Cursor speak to you in a voice you choose.

Models and voice data never leave your machine. There are installers for Apple silicon and Intel Macs and for Windows; Linux users build from source.

whatPeopleSay.summary:
Most of what's written about Voicebox is enthusiastic: people see it as a free, local-first alternative to ElevenLabs, and like that voice samples never leave their own computer and that several speech engines sit behind one tidy app. Hands-on criticism comes mostly from GitHub issues: early Windows builds didn't use the GPU, first-run guidance was thin, and the open-issue list is long. It also needs a fairly strong machine. Independent tests of its quality against ElevenLabs are still scarce.

Hacker News coverage is light (mostly passing recommendations), and we couldn't check Reddit for this round-up.

Several speech engines, voice cloning and dictation in one app
Free and MIT-licensed, with extras like a multi-speaker story editor and an MCP server for AI agents
Polished interface and well-thought-out dictation

Bugs and thin onboarding reported, with a large issue backlog

projects.description: A gym and body-weight tracker you host yourself: plan routines, log every set and watch your progress, synced across your phone and laptop.
projects.longDescription:
Plan a routine for each weekday (or a rotation) from a library of over 5,600 exercises with animated demos and a body map, or start from one of four ready-made plans. During a workout, weights are filled in from last time, a rest timer runs between sets and personal records are spotted as you go. It handles supersets, drop sets, timed and cardio exercises, and works out plate math from the plates your gym has.

You run it on your own server with one docker compose command; it installs to the home screen, works offline and signs in with passkeys. There is an Android APK, an iPhone and Apple Watch app, and a live demo in the browser. No account on anyone else's server, no subscription, no ads.

projects.name: SolidCraft
projects.description: A free parametric 3D CAD app: sketch, constrain and build solids on a feature timeline, then change a dimension and watch the model rebuild. For Windows, Mac, Linux and the web.
projects.longDescription:
SolidCraft has sketches with its own constraint solver, and extrude, revolve, sweep, loft, fillet, chamfer, shell, holes, threads and patterns on an editable timeline. It also does parameters and configurations, assemblies with joints and motion studies, and sheet metal with flat patterns. It opens and saves STEP, IGES, 3MF, STL, OBJ and glTF.

Its README calls it early but usable for simple parts. There are installers for Windows, Mac (signed and notarized) and Linux (AppImage, Snap and more), and a version that runs in the browser. A command-line tool and MCP server run the same commands.

projects.description: A small, fast DNS server and ad blocker for your home network that shows which device asked for what and why each answer was given. Runs on a Raspberry Pi or any Linux machine.

projects.name: Legends of Future Past
projects.description: An award-winning 1992 online text adventure from CompuServe, lost when it shut down in 1999 and rebuilt by its original creator from the surviving game scripts. Free to play in your browser.
projects.longDescription:
Legends of Future Past was one of the first commercial online multiplayer games, a text world (a MUD) set in the Shattered Realms of Andor with eight races, five schools of magic, psionic combat and over two thousand rooms. Computer Gaming World gave it a Special Award for Artistic Excellence in 1993.

The original engine's source code was lost, but former Game Masters had kept the script files that define every room, item, monster and quest. The new engine runs those original scripts, so the world is the real one. The server is free to play, and you can host your own copy.
projects.builtWithAI: Jon Radoff, who made the original game in 1992, says in the README that he used Claude Code to reconstruct it from the old script files, manuals and captured play sessions, in a weekend of agentic engineering. Checked 2026-11-22: all 120 commits are co-authored by Claude.

whatPeopleSay.summary: The AI-assisted revival got notable attention in Chinese tech and games media, which framed it as a 1990s online game brought back in a weekend with Claude. A 17173 writer who played it said the game beat their expectations and felt immersive despite being text only, though the lack of Chinese support was a hurdle. Former players commenting on the maker's write-up were mostly nostalgic and grateful, with one doubting the 'one weekend' framing.

Reviewer found the text-only game surprisingly immersive with plenty of content
Seen as a striking example of AI-assisted software preservation

projects.name: DBackup
projects.alternative: Alternative to hosted database backup services
projects.description: Self-hosted backup automation for databases and files: scheduled, encrypted, compressed backups to the storage you choose, with restores in a few clicks.
projects.longDescription:
DBackup backs up 10 kinds of database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis, Firebird and more, directly or over SSH) together with the files that belong to them, then sends them to 13 kinds of storage such as S3, cloud drives, SFTP, SMB and WebDAV. It runs as one Docker container. Backups are standard dumps and TAR archives encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and a Recovery Kit decrypts them without DBackup. It has SSO, permissions, 2FA, passkeys and an audit log for teams.

projects.name: Tab Out
projects.description: A Chrome extension that turns your new tab page into a dashboard of every open tab, grouped by site, so you can jump to one or close a whole group at once.
projects.longDescription:
Tab Out shows your open tabs on a clean grid, grouped by domain, with homepages such as Gmail, YouTube and GitHub pulled into their own group. It flags duplicate tabs, lets you click a tab to jump straight to it in any window, and has a save-for-later list. Closing a group plays a swoosh with confetti.

Everything stays on your computer: no server, no account and no outside calls. You install it in Chrome as an unpacked extension (Developer mode, Load unpacked), or ask a coding agent to set it up for you.

projects.name: Ink Away
projects.alternative: Alternative to Kindle Scribe and reMarkable notebooks
projects.description: A drawing, handwritten notes and book annotation add-on for KOReader on Kindle, Kobo and Android e-readers, with pen pressure, palm rejection and PDF export.
projects.longDescription:
Ink Away adds a pen to KOReader, the free e-book reader that runs on jailbroken Kindles, Kobos and Android. You can draw with many pens (fineliner, fountain, pencil, watercolor and smudge) on up to five layers, keep notebooks on lined, grid or planner pages with handwriting turned into text, and write on any book KOReader opens, with the ink following its words when you change the font size.

Books you have written on can be exported as PDFs that keep your ink and searchable text. It needs a stylus-capable reader; palm rejection needs KOReader 2026.07 or newer. Install it by copying the folder into KOReader's plugins directory.

projects.name: ROM Librarian
projects.description: A desktop app for tidying retro game ROM collections: batch rename with No-Intro DATs, compress to ZIP or 7z, convert disc images to CHD and keep EmulationStation lists in sync.
projects.longDescription:
ROM Librarian has tabs for each cleanup job. Rename uses regular expressions and presets to strip region and dump tags, with a live preview and undo. DAT Rename matches files (even inside ZIPs) against No-Intro DAT files by CRC32, MD5 and SHA1. Compression batch-packs or unpacks ZIP and 7z, and Conversion turns CUE/BIN and ISO disc images into compressed CHD files for MAME and RetroArch.

Renames also update EmulationStation/RetroPie gamelist.xml files and the CUE sheets that point at BIN files. The Windows build is a portable zip with no Python needed; Linux runs it from source and has a command-line mode. It is for organizing games you own.

projects.name: Emberwick
projects.description: A top-down 3D fantasy role-playing game in the browser with a story, companions, quests and a built-in level editor. Free to play, nothing to install.
projects.longDescription:
Emberwick is an original fantasy adventure: explore a 3D world from above, talk to characters, take on quests with companions and follow its plot. It also has a level editor. It runs in a desktop browser.

Its maker wrote about building it, and about how much better AI-made games got in October 2026, on his blog at simonwillison.net.

projects.name: Quarter Sun Cove
projects.description: A cozy isometric farming game in the browser: grow pumpkins, tend your farm and meet a town of animal characters. Free to play, nothing to install.
projects.longDescription:
Quarter Sun Cove (first called Pumpkin Farmer) is a relaxed farming sim seen from an isometric view. You plant and grow pumpkins and get to know the animal characters who live around the cove. Its maker set out to make something original rather than an imitation of an existing farming game.

The written spec it was built from is published on GitHub, and the story of how it was made is on simonwillison.net.

projects.name: Starfall
projects.description: A 3D space real-time strategy game in the browser: build and command fleets from scouts to a two-kilometre mothership in full 3D, against a computer opponent.
projects.longDescription:
Starfall has thirteen ship classes, true 3D movement with a move disc for setting altitude, formations, stances and control groups, plus production, research, resource harvesting and an AI opponent. Every hull, planet, nebula and effect is generated in code at runtime, so there are no image files at all; the only bought-in assets are free (CC0) sounds and music.

It is an original game in the style of the classic 3D space strategy games, not a copy: it uses none of their art, sound, code or names. It needs a desktop browser with WebGL 2.

projects.name: SetShot
projects.alternative: Alternative to keeping notes on your Mac's settings by hand
projects.description: A Mac app that snapshots hundreds of macOS settings and compares two snapshots, so you can see exactly what an update, an installer or you changed, explained in plain English.
projects.longDescription:
Take a snapshot, change something (apply a macOS update, install software, adjust preferences), then take another. SetShot lists the recognized changes with a plain-English description, where to find each one in System Settings and, where possible, an Open in Settings button. Unrecognized changes show the raw name and old and new values, and can be submitted to grow its knowledge base.

A journal keeps a searchable history of every change, snapshots can run on a schedule in the background, and you can compare against built-in baselines of fresh macOS 15, 26 and 27 installs to export everything you've changed. It never changes settings itself, and snapshots stay on your Mac. Runs on macOS 13 Ventura and later.

projects.name: Parenthèse
projects.description: A family tree you explore like a map, with photos, videos and voice recordings on every person, shared with relatives by a link and a password. Free to use online or self-host.
projects.longDescription:
Each person in the tree can hold photos, videos, audio recordings, documents and GPS tracks, and you can draw, add stickers or place photos anywhere on the tree. Relatives who get the link and password look around without an account and can suggest additions, which the owner can apply straight away or review first. GEDCOM import and export lets you move from or to other genealogy programs.

There is a hosted version at app.parenthese.io (with a demo that needs no account) and a Docker setup for running your own copy on a server or NAS. The interface is in English, French and German. The code is source-available under a non-commercial licence, not an OSI open source licence.

projects.name: Mailflare
projects.description: Self-hosted email on your own domain, plus calendar, booking links and file storage, that runs on Cloudflare or in one Docker container. Receiving and sending can be free.
projects.longDescription:
Mailflare gives you personal or shared mailboxes on custom domains, routing rules to store, forward, reject or sort mail, a calendar with time zones and email invitations, a public booking page, and a Drive for storing and sharing files. Built-in AI agents can search mail, draft replies and manage events. You can import mail from IMAP, Gmail Takeout, .eml and .mbox files, and the interface comes in 34 languages.

It deploys to Cloudflare Workers with one button or runs as a single Docker container, with a choice of databases (Cloudflare D1, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and others) and storage (R2, B2 or S3). Receiving through Cloudflare Email Routing is free and sending can use the free tiers of Resend or Amazon SES. A hosted Mailflare Cloud is also offered from $4.

projects.name: FluidWin
projects.description: Reshapes Windows 11 with a dock that replaces the taskbar, a notch that shows the time, volume, music and notifications, and a glass control center. Close it and Windows goes back exactly as it was.
projects.longDescription:
The dock shows your apps with notification badges, live window previews, jump-list commands, a Downloads stack and the Recycle Bin, and can sit on any edge of the screen or follow you to another monitor. The notch at the top grows to show volume, notifications, the song playing with its controls and a timer, and has a shelf you can drag files onto. The control center groups Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, dark theme, keep awake, silent mode, timer, calendar, weather and news.

It is a portable zip with nothing to install, it never changes Windows system files, and it checks for updates itself. It is a one-person hobby project.

projects.name: OldPhoneDeck
projects.description: Turns an old iPhone or iPad into a Stream Deck style control panel for your Mac, with app keys, now playing, Mac controls and widgets. Runs in Safari, with no jailbreak and no App Store.
projects.longDescription:
A menu bar app on the Mac (PhoneDeck.app) has a Command Center where you drag apps, widgets and controls onto pages for an iPhone 4S, a modern iPhone or an iPad mini. Keys open any Mac app with its Dock badge, control Spotify or Apple Music, volume, brightness, dark mode, window tiling, Focus and even an external monitor's input. Widgets include clock, weather, calendar, Mac performance, batteries and handwritten notes.

It works on devices as old as an iPhone 4S on iOS 9, and a phone can also serve as a webcam and mic for calls or as a small second display. You build the Mac app from source with one script (macOS 14 or later and the Xcode command line tools).

projects.name: Game Glance
projects.alternative: Alternative to Steam's Game Mode home, HLTB for Deck
projects.description: A Decky Loader plugin for Steam's Game Mode on handhelds that turns each game's page into a full-screen view with how long it takes to beat, play time and achievements, plus an optional new home screen.
projects.longDescription:
The game page shows full-screen art, HowLongToBeat times, your play time and achievements, and where the game comes from. Spotlight Home (off by default) replaces Steam's Home with one game at a time over its art, a row of recent games, all installed games including non-Steam ones, and Friends, News and Recommended tabs. It also adds touch and mouse control, a screensaver drawn from your games, and store info for games added by Heroic.

Install it from Game Mode through Decky's Install plugin from URL; it updates itself from releases. It was tested on a ROG Xbox Ally running Bazzite and should work on a Steam Deck and other SteamOS-like devices.

projects.name: Halcyon
projects.alternative: Inspired by open-world island exploration games
projects.description: A tropical atoll that lives through a whole day in your browser: walk the beach, swim the reef, sail the lagoon and fly over the peak, from sunrise to a glowing night.
projects.longDescription:
Everything is drawn live with three.js and WebGL2: an FFT ocean that breaks on the reef, a 330 m peak built from real lidar, 43,000 scanned plants and 370,000 coral colonies, whales, dolphins, turtles and schools of fish, and a 36-minute day whose weather changes by itself before the lagoon lights up with bioluminescence.

It is a calm place to explore rather than a game with goals, made to the standard of a game's hero shot and kept at 60 fps on a laptop. It is from the maker of Neon Zenith and Sakura Fantasy. The code is MIT; models, textures and fonts keep their own licences.

projects.name: OpenAero DFW
projects.description: A flight simulator in the browser over real satellite imagery of Dallas-Fort Worth: fly a Boeing 737, a Cessna 172 or an F-16 in today's real weather and get every landing graded.
projects.longDescription:
It is a six-degrees-of-freedom flight model flown over the whole Dallas-Fort Worth area: land a 737 on DFW 35C, take an F-16 past Reunion Tower, or fly the approach into Love Field in a Cessna. Weather comes from the current METAR report. There is no install and no account, with keyboard controls (pitch, roll, rudder, throttle, gear, flaps, brakes, autopilot, mouse yoke) and touch controls on phones and tablets.

A player guide on the site explains the controls and approaches.
